articles.title: ‘His Weakest Creatures’ Director on Offering Hope to Egyptians With His Feel-Good Crime Comedy, Starring Ahmed Helmy and Hend Sabry
articles.summary: Egyptian filmmaker Omar Hilal (“Voy! Voy! Voy!”) unites two of the Arab film world’s most bankable stars in his latest feature, “His Weakest Creatures,” a dark comedic thriller that premiered with a gala screening Friday at the Marrakech Film Festival.
body: Co-written by the director and his brother Ahmed Hilal, the film is produced by Cairo-based Film Clinic and Dubai-based Front Row Filmed Entertainment — who previously collaborated on the local remake of “Perfect Strangers,” the first Arabic-language Netflix original — along with HWC Productions, Film Square, Arabia Pictures and Block 8, in association with Sinai Studios. Front Row is handling the film’s international sales.

“His Weakest Creatures” was inspired by the incredible, pulled-from-the-headlines story of a spate of mysterious disappearances that took place at the Giza Zoo between 2005 and 2008, when an estimated 400 animals were stolen.

As with the director’s previous effort, which represented Egypt in the 2024 Oscar race for best international feature, the film focuses on the travails of everyday Egyptians whose fortunes have steadily eroded, along with their hopes for returning their struggling nation to its former glory.

articles.title: ‘Clarissa’ Directing Duo on How Sophie Okonedo and Star-Studded Ensemble Brought Neon’s Lagos-Set ‘Mrs. Dalloway’ Adaptation to Life
articles.summary: It’s been a whirlwind year for Chuko and Arie Esiri, the breakout Nigerian directing duo whose star-studded, Lagos-set “Mrs. Dalloway” reinterpretation “Clarissa” wowed audiences at this year’s Cannes Film Festival.
body: A reimagining of Virginia Woolf’s classic novel, “Clarissa” follows a society woman as she prepares to host a party at her home in Lagos, where she’ll unexpectedly encounter once-intimate friends from her youth. Reviewing the film in Cannes, Variety ’s Jessica Kiang heralded the Esiri duo’s “quietly dazzling Nigerian reinterpretation of ‘Mrs. Dalloway,’” praising “a superb Sophie Okonedo, radiant with melancholy, at the heart of its remarkably well-cast ensemble,” which includes David Oyelowo (“Selma”), India Amarteifio (“Queen Charlotte”), Ayo Edebiri (“The Bear”) and Toheeb Jimoh (“Ted Lasso,” “Industry”).

“Expanding in ambition and feeling from their promising debut ‘ This Is My Desire ’ (aka ‘Eyimofe’),” wrote Kiang, “the Esiris cast a perceptive eye over the elite social constellation that has fallen into orbit around this dutiful but unfulfilled society wife, and have nothing but compassion for her as she spins slowly around and around at its center: loved by some, resented by others, admired by all — and totally alone.”

articles.title: Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival Opens With Lawrence Fajardo’s ‘Silenced Nights’ and a Call to Face Reality
articles.summary: The 21st Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival (JAFF) kicked off Nov. 28 at the Empire XXI cinema in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, with Filipino director Lawrence Fajardo’s thriller “Silenced Nights” as its opening film. The evening’s gentle drizzle stopped shortly after the ceremony began.
body: The ceremony then took a political turn. Festival president Ifa Isfansyah and festival director Budi Irawanto invited the audience to reflect on the unsettling state of the world, pointing to natural and political crises and social inequality that threaten people’s safety.

“A festival must not be a space separate from reality; it cannot just be a place to escape from problems out there. Instead, a festival must be a space to face reality, open up conversations, bring together various perspectives, and preserve the possibility of critical thinking,” said Irawanto, who then asked attendees to stand for a moment of silence.

Fajardo thanked the festival and said the film is personally meaningful to him. “Silenced Nights,” set against extrajudicial killings in a Philippine urban community, played in the Platform competition at the Toronto International Film Festival in September.

Indonesian singer Mondo Gascaro closed the night with a live set that opened with the soothing “Butiran Angin” and took in “Senandung Lagu Lama,” from Usmar Ismail’s 1956 musical “Tiga Dara” (“Three Maidens”); “Apatis,” composed for Nugroho’s “Kucumbu Tubuh Indahku” (“Memories of My Body”); and “Dan Bila.”

articles.title: Scout Willis, Will Peltz and Kurt Deimer to Star in Indie Thriller ‘The Prostitute’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Scout Willis, Will Peltz and Kurt Deimer lead the cast of writer-director Paul Boyd’s dark psychological thriller “The Prostitute.” The indie film stars Peltz (“Euphoria,” “Manifest,” “Unfriended”) as a young, struggling filmmaker living out of his van in Hollywood who becomes fixated on…
body: Principal photography is underway, and the film will shoot entirely in Los Angeles. Eric Barrett is producing for Mirror Films, and Deimer (“Halloween 2018,” “Scared to Death,” “Hellbilly Hollow,” “Trading Paint”) is executive producing through his Bald Man Films banner.
Blending found-footage intimacy with narrative intensity, “The Prostitute” explores the dark intersection of content creation, voyeurism and true-crime obsession in modern Los Angeles.

“This is a raw, unsettling story about the cost of chasing a story,” Boyd (“Scared to Death,” “Vicious Circle”) said in a statement. “We’re thrilled to have this cast in front of the camera, exploring the thin line between art and exploitation on the streets of Los Angeles.”

Barrett added, “Paul has written a provocative and timely thriller that feels both intimate and explosive. Pairing him with this cast and Kurt’s genre expertise through Bald Man Films creates the perfect team to bring ‘The Prostitute’ to the screen.”

articles.title: ‘Who asked that? You should be ashamed of yourself!’: Judi Dench answers questions from Ian McKellen, Lorraine Kelly, David Hare and more
articles.summary: Fans and famous friends put their nosiest questions to the 91-year-old actor. It’s mid-afternoon and Judi Dench and I are sitting in the “den” of her country house in Surrey.
body: Behind Judi’s head hangs an enormous painting of her as M, presented as a gift on her last day of filming on Skyfall. Through the latticed windows is a view on to the garden, which is crowded with trees she plants for lost friends and family – a beloved oak, a tribute to her late husband, actor Michael Williams, towers above the pond. Even though the room is suffused with autumn sunshine, all the lights are on in the house. Judi has always needed light around her – she’s been afraid of the dark since she was small.

Deflecting and mucking about is Judi’s modus operandi. It’s not an end in itself – it’s her process, and it’s also how she works as an actor. Games help to bond a company and build relationships. But for Judi they serve an additional purpose – they are a necessary step towards accessing something deeper, more profound within herself. She describes it as taking the froth off the beer in order to reach what’s beneath. Eventually, today, we get stuck into our Q&A – and things are just as lively as in the run-up.

articles.title: Watching Wild Horse Nine in Santiago brings Pinochet’s tyranny back to dreadful life
articles.summary: Having lived through the real life horror it was chilling to see Martin McDonagh’s film so close to its historical site. Would its audience hear the urgent message? It was chilling for me, as a survivor of the 1973 coup that installed a bloody 17-year dictatorship in Chile, to watch Wild Horse Nine…
body: Though Martin McDonagh’s film is set shortly before the military takeover, it disturbingly foretells the atrocities that are to come, a terrifying future that is known to the protagonists, Chris and Lee, because, as CIA agents, they have been instrumental in the conspiracy to destroy the peaceful revolution of democratically elected president Salvador Allende.

Chris (John Malkovich, in a stunning performance) is dying of cancer and saturated with regrets about his interventions in other lands that were once democratic. On a trip to Easter Island where he has gone to spend his last days, he meets Mónica (Mariana di Girolamo), an idealistic leftwing Chilean student. Beguiled by her (“She is life. And I am leaving it.”), he gradually reveals not only his own clandestine identity and the date of the coup, 11 September, but the fate that awaits Allendistas like her who will be rounded up, taken to a soccer stadium to be tortured and, some of them, executed.

articles.title: Actor and comedian PJ Gallagher dies aged 51
articles.summary: PJ Gallagher appeared on Irish television for more than two decades with shows including Naked Camera and The Young Offenders.
body: Taoiseach (Irish prime minster) Micheál Martin has led tributes to comedian and broadcaster PJ Gallagher, who has died at the age of 51.
Born in Cork and adopted and raised in Dublin, Gallagher was a familiar presence on television for more than two decades, appearing in numerous programmes, including BBC's The Young Offenders.
He first came to prominence in 2005, co-creating the RTÉ hidden-camera series Naked Camera, which established him as one of Ireland's best-known comedy performers.
As well as his work in stand-up comedy and acting, Gallagher presented television documentaries and was a member of the breakfast show team on Radio Nova.

articles.title: Take That say 10th number one album feels as special as first
articles.summary: The Manchester group has topped the UK album chart with Dreamers.
body: Take That have landed their 10th number one album, securing their spot as one of the most successful British bands in Official Chart history.
The group first scored a number one record more than three decades ago with their second studio album Everything Changes.
The band told Official Charts: "Thank you so much to everybody who has supported Dreamers, it means the world to us to see people embracing this album.
"Thinking back to our first number one with Everything Changes in 1993, this one today feels even more special.

articles.title: Babydoll singer lands longest-running UK number one by Welsh artist in 56 years
articles.summary: Jamie Miller, originally from Cardiff, claims the top spot in the UK singles chart for the sixth week.
body: Jamie Miller's Babydoll has become the longest-running UK number one single by a Welsh artist in 56 years.
Miller, who is originally from Pontprennau in Cardiff, claimed the top spot with his TikTok-viral hit for the sixth consecutive week on Friday.
The 29-year-old star's success is equal to the six-week streak set by Dave Edmunds' I Hear You Knocking back in 1970.
Babydoll was released on 7 August - just months after Miller considered quitting music - and exploded after actress Jennifer Love Hewitt and other stars posted videos which featured the track.

articles.title: Roger Ebert Named This Panned Nicolas Cage Thriller One Of The Best Sci-Fi Action Movies Ever
articles.summary: Roger Ebert was drawn to the big themes in this Nicolas Cage-led sci-fi flick, even as other critics were put off by its wild ideas and general silliness.
body: Most critics hated Alex Proyas' 2009 film "Knowing," and I haven't heard much mention of it in the years since its release. At the same time, it was something of a box office hit, and it even had Roger Ebert in its corner. Awarding the film four stars (out of four), Ebert called it "one of the best science fiction movies I've ever seen." Ebert was famously a sci-fi aficionado who often gave perfect ratings to unexpected examples of the genre, so his review is high praise indeed.

Looking over the premise, one might be able to intuit why so many critics rejected "Knowing." It's an ambitious and somewhat gonzo sci-fi thriller about John Koestler (Nicolas Cage), an astrophysics professor who finds a 50-year-old string of numbers that, when interpreted correctly, seemingly point to future disasters and cataclysms. Koestler tries to prevent said cataclysms, but he's unsuccessful. In other words, he bears the weight of knowing about the future, yet he's powerless to prevent it.

articles.title: Jake Bugg reflects on 'vulnerable' new album he almost didn't release
articles.summary: The singer, who had a number one with his first album, says his latest reflects tough years since.
body: Jake Bugg says writing his latest album was an opportunity to explore loss, regrets and the lessons he has learned along the way.
After enjoying success with his self-titled debut album in 2012, the Nottingham singer says he has since struggled to maintain relationships and ended up feeling isolated.
Despite such a personal record potentially leaving him "very vulnerable", he decided "if somebody can take a slight bit of comfort in this record then the music's bigger than myself".
Best known for the single Lightning Bolt, Bugg released six albums between 2012 and 2024.
